title: Total thyroidectomy
text: Total thyroidectomy. In this film we follow the operation step by step on a three dimensional model of the neck, from the skin incision to closure, and look closely at the structures that are at risk along the way.

title: Position and incision
text: The patient lies supine, with the neck extended on a shoulder roll and the head resting on a ring. If nerve monitoring is used, check that the electrodes on the tube sit at the vocal folds. A Kocher collar incision is made in, or close to, a skin crease, about two fingers' breadth above the sternal notch. It is usually four to six centimetres long.

title: Subplatysmal flaps
text: Platysma is divided, and flaps are raised deep to it, but superficial to the anterior jugular veins. The upper flap is raised to the notch of the thyroid cartilage, and the lower flap down to the sternal notch.

title: Open the midline
text: The avascular midline raphe between the sternohyoid muscles is opened, from the thyroid cartilage down to the sternal notch. Sternothyroid is separated from the lobe, and the strap muscles are retracted laterally. They are divided high only if the gland is very large.

title: Middle thyroid vein and vagus
text: The lobe is rolled forwards and medially. The middle thyroid vein is ligated, opening the space between the lobe and the carotid sheath. With nerve monitoring, the vagus is stimulated inside the sheath to record a baseline signal.

title: Upper pole
text: The upper pole is drawn downwards and laterally, opening the space between the gland and cricothyroid. Look for the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve on the inferior constrictor. The superior thyroid artery and vein are ligated branch by branch on the capsule, rather than as a mass higher up, to protect this nerve.

title: Parathyroids
text: The superior parathyroid lies near the cricothyroid junction, behind the upper part of the lobe. The inferior parathyroid lies near the lower pole. Each is swept off the capsule together with its own blood supply, and the branches of the inferior thyroid artery are divided on the capsule, beyond the branches to the parathyroids.

title: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
text: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is found low down, in Simon's triangle, bounded by the common carotid artery, the trachea and oesophagus, and the inferior thyroid artery. It can also be found where it crosses that artery, or beneath the tubercle of Zuckerkandl. The right nerve runs obliquely, while the left runs more vertically in the tracheo-oesophageal groove. It is traced upwards to the cricothyroid joint.

title: Berry's ligament
text: With the nerve in view, Berry's ligament is divided under direct vision, with fine clips or ties. Energy devices and blind clamping are avoided here, because this is where most nerve injuries happen. The inferior thyroid veins are divided at the lower pole, and the lobe is lifted off the trachea.

title: Isthmus and the other side
text: The isthmus is divided off the trachea, including any pyramidal lobe, and the same steps are repeated on the other side. If the monitoring signal was lost on the first side, consider stopping, and completing the second side later, to avoid injuring both nerves.

title: Check and close
text: The vagus is stimulated again at the end. The parathyroids are inspected, and any that are dark, or were removed, are autotransplanted after the tissue is confirmed. A Valsalva manoeuvre checks haemostasis. The strap muscles are closed loosely in the midline, so that a haematoma can come forwards, followed by platysma and skin.

title: Structures at risk
text: To summarise, the structures at risk are both recurrent laryngeal nerves, a non-recurrent nerve on the right side, the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve, and the parathyroid glands. This film is for education only. Always check surgical detail against current atlases and senior guidance.
